## Loading Libraries

```{r}
library("tidyverse")
library("janitor")
library("patchwork")
library("broom")
library("curl")
library("here")
```

## Loading Augmented File

```{r}
brca <- read_csv(here("data", "brca_augment.csv"),
                     na = c("", "NA", "N/A", "?", "null"))
```

## Visualization

### Visualization 1 - Bar Plot

```{r}
brca |>
  drop_na(type_of_breast_surgery,
          cancer_type_short,
          cellularity) |>
  ggplot(aes(x = cancer_type_short,
             fill = type_of_breast_surgery)) +
  geom_bar(position = "fill",
           width = 0.65,
           color = "white") +
  facet_wrap(~ cellularity) +
  scale_y_continuous(labels = scales::percent) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = c("plum", "lightpink")) +
  labs(title = "Surgery Type by Cancer Type & Cellularity",
       x = NULL,
       y = "Patients (%)",
       fill = "Surgery") +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 10) +
  theme(axis.text.x = element_text(size = 8,
                                   angle = 30,
                                   hjust = 1),
        legend.position = "bottom")
```

Across all cancer types and cellularity levels, **mastectomy** is consistently more common than breast-conserving surgery, accounting for roughly 55%–72% of patients in every group. Patients with **ILC** show the highest proportion of mastectomies across all three cellularity panels (peaking above 70% in moderate cellularity). Overall, higher tumor cellularity does not appear to drive a clear increase in mastectomy rates, as the surgery proportions remain fairly stable from low to high cellularity.
